title: Fortinet Enterprise Networking & Security — 50-question graded examination

questions.question: After an 8.0 upgrade, FortiGuard begins alternating across more first-choice servers. Which setting explains the change?

choices.text: The update schedule now selects servers by antivirus package age.
choices.feedback: Package age affects update eligibility, not the configured server-pool size.

choices.text: The unset load-balance-servers value now defaults to five candidates. now
choices.feedback: Correct: an unset value changes from one to five in 8.0.

choices.text: The FortiGate Cloud account automatically adds five custom servers. now
choices.feedback: Cloud registration does not silently create five custom server entries.

choices.text: The rating service now ignores configured public-server preference. for this service
choices.feedback: Rating preference is service-specific and does not explain this default.

questions.question: IPS packages download successfully, but web filtering reports rating-server failures. What should be checked first?

choices.text: The IPS package checksum and antivirus engine version. for this service
choices.feedback: Package integrity does not establish rating-service reachability.

choices.text: The FortiGate session table and SD-WAN load-balance algorithm. for this service
choices.feedback: Session hashing does not select FortiGuard rating endpoints.

choices.text: The rating server's FortiToken assignment and user group. for this service
choices.feedback: FortiToken state is unrelated to the FortiGuard rating service.

choices.text: Whether a custom server is assigned the Filtering service type.
choices.feedback: Correct: custom servers are service-type-specific; update success is not rating success.

questions.question: The GUI omits “Always use custom” after a management change. Which evidence is most useful?

choices.text: Full central-management settings and FortiGate Cloud configuration. now
choices.feedback: Correct: central-management/FortiGate Cloud state affects available preference choices.

choices.text: The IPS signature database timestamp and package checksum.
choices.feedback: Signature freshness cannot explain a hidden server-preference option.

choices.text: The firewall policy sequence number and NAT table.
choices.feedback: Policy order and NAT state are separate from FortiGuard preference UI.

choices.text: The web-filter category database version and cache age.
choices.feedback: Category database age is not the controlling GUI dependency.

questions.question: What does load-balance-servers control in the FortiGuard selection process?

choices.text: The maximum number of active firewall sessions per WAN member.
choices.feedback: Firewall session capacity is not controlled by this FortiGuard setting.

choices.text: The number of custom servers permitted in the central-management list.
choices.feedback: Custom server-list size is a separate configuration concern.

choices.text: The count of first-choice FortiGuard servers used for round-robin selection.
choices.feedback: Correct: it sets how many first-choice servers participate in round-robin.

choices.text: The number of FortiGate Cloud tenants sharing one update proxy.
choices.feedback: Cloud tenant count is not the setting's documented purpose.

questions.question: A custom FortiGuard endpoint appears in the list but is never used for rating. What is likely wrong?

choices.text: Its server-type assignment does not include Filtering. for this service
choices.feedback: Correct: a server must be assigned to the service it is expected to provide.

choices.text: Its IPv4 address is outside the branch user subnet.
choices.feedback: The endpoint need not be inside the user subnet.

choices.text: Its DNS name is absent from the web-filter allowlist.
choices.feedback: A web-filter allowlist does not assign FortiGuard server roles.

choices.text: Its SSL-VPN portal does not reference the endpoint. now
choices.feedback: SSL-VPN portal configuration is unrelated to rating-server selection.

questions.question: Two branches need the same local username but different passwords and FortiToken bindings. What should be configured?

choices.text: Two separate ADOMs with duplicate user objects and policies. for that device
choices.feedback: Duplicate ADOMs are unnecessary when device-scoped mappings are supported.

choices.text: One ADOM local user with per-device mappings for each FortiGate. here
choices.feedback: Correct: one parent local user can carry per-device authentication overrides.

choices.text: A shared LDAP group with one password and one token serial.
choices.feedback: LDAP group membership does not create local password/token overrides.

choices.text: A FortiGate Cloud account for each branch authentication realm. for that device
choices.feedback: FortiGate Cloud accounts do not implement this FortiManager object model.

questions.question: Install preview shows the headquarters token on a branch FortiGate. Which check is most targeted?

choices.text: Confirm the user object is in the global root ADOM only.
choices.feedback: The ADOM scope matters, but the reported symptom points to mapping selection.

choices.text: Recreate the branch policy package with a new policy ID. here
choices.feedback: A new policy ID does not repair authentication mapping.

choices.text: Reset every FortiToken before comparing device configuration. on the target FortiGate
choices.feedback: Bulk token resets are disruptive and do not prove mapping selection.

choices.text: Inspect that device's Per-Device Mapping entry and install target. for that device
choices.feedback: Correct: verify the branch-specific mapping and the device receiving it.

questions.question: The mapping is correct and installation succeeded, but the user still cannot authenticate. What is next?

choices.text: Verify the target FortiGate local user and actual token activation.
choices.feedback: Correct: installed local configuration and token state are now the next boundary.

choices.text: Rebuild the FortiManager ADOM database and policy object cache. here
choices.feedback: A database rebuild is not justified by a local authentication failure.

choices.text: Change the parent username to a different global identity. here
choices.feedback: Changing the parent identity can affect every device mapping.

choices.text: Disable all branch two-factor authentication until login succeeds. for that device
choices.feedback: Disabling MFA masks the issue and weakens security.

questions.question: Does per-device mapping make a FortiGate consult FortiManager during each user login?

choices.text: Yes; FortiManager proxies each password challenge to the device. here
choices.feedback: FortiManager does not act as a live authentication proxy here.

choices.text: Yes; the mapping is queried through a persistent ADOM session.
choices.feedback: An ADOM session is not the runtime login path.

choices.text: No; FortiManager renders device-specific configuration during installation. in this ADOM
choices.feedback: Correct: the target FortiGate authenticates using its installed local configuration.

choices.text: No; the FortiGate ignores the local user after installation. here
choices.feedback: The local user remains the authentication object on the FortiGate.

questions.question: After a 7.6 upgrade, analytics storage shrinks from 4 TB to 100 GB. What proves data loss?

choices.text: A smaller ClickHouse footprint by itself. for the same archived interval
choices.feedback: Compression and cache regeneration can reduce disk usage substantially.

choices.text: An older first-log timestamp and lower daily counts for expected periods.
choices.feedback: Correct: date range and per-day counts test actual analytics completeness.

choices.text: A regenerated hcache table with a different row count. for this ADOM
choices.feedback: Hcache is regenerated on demand and is not a raw-log count.

choices.text: A new database engine name in the upgrade log. for this ADOM
choices.feedback: An engine-name change is expected during migration.

questions.question: What is the documented sequencing dependency during the PostgreSQL-to-ClickHouse upgrade?

choices.text: ClickHouse migration completes before FortiGate schema updates begin. for this ADOM
choices.feedback: This reverses the documented order.

choices.text: All ADOM reports rebuild before the PostgreSQL schema changes. now
choices.feedback: Report rebuild is not the prerequisite stage described.

choices.text: FortiGate log-schema updates complete in PostgreSQL before migration begins. now
choices.feedback: Correct: schema alignment in PostgreSQL precedes the migration.

choices.text: Archive logs are deleted before the ClickHouse database is initialized.
choices.feedback: Archive logs are the recovery source and should not be deleted first.

questions.question: A historical interval is genuinely missing after migration. What determines whether rebuild can restore it?

choices.text: Whether raw archive logs for that interval are still retained.
choices.feedback: Correct: rebuild re-inserts raw archive logs; absent archives cannot be recreated.

choices.text: Whether the ClickHouse database occupies the old disk size. now
choices.feedback: Disk footprint is not a completeness criterion.

choices.text: Whether the FortiGate has a current IPS signature package. now
choices.feedback: IPS package freshness is unrelated to archived analytics history.

choices.text: Whether the ADOM has at least one dashboard widget. now
choices.feedback: Dashboard presence does not restore missing raw data.

questions.question: What does diagnose sql status rebuild-db establish during the recovery process?

choices.text: Whether the FortiGate log schema is still being edited.
choices.feedback: The command does not report FortiGate schema editing.

choices.text: Whether all reports have been exported to CSV. now
choices.feedback: CSV export is a separate reporting operation.

choices.text: Whether the archive quota is automatically sufficient. for this ADOM
choices.feedback: Archive quota must be checked independently.

choices.text: The current analytics database rebuild status. during migration
choices.feedback: Correct: it reports the rebuild state, not archive sufficiency.

questions.question: Why should a full rebuild be treated as a maintenance operation in 7.6?

choices.text: It only refreshes one report cache without affecting other ADOMs.
choices.feedback: The documented rebuild is broader than one report cache.

choices.text: It reboots and rebuilds analytics across ADOMs from archived logs.
choices.feedback: Correct: it reboots and rebuilds all ADOM analytics from archives.

choices.text: It permanently deletes the raw archive log files. for this ADOM
choices.feedback: Archive logs are the source and should remain available.

choices.text: It converts the FortiGate device database into ClickHouse. for this ADOM
choices.feedback: The migration concerns FortiAnalyzer analytics, not the FortiGate device database.

questions.question: FortiSwitch uses DoT but no server-ca-cert is configured. What security property remains unproven?

choices.text: That the resolver's certificate chains to a trusted CA.
choices.feedback: Correct: TLS encryption without a configured CA does not authenticate resolver identity.

choices.text: That the switch can open TCP/853 to the resolver.
choices.feedback: TCP/853 reachability can still be present.

choices.text: That DNS messages are encapsulated in TLS. over TLS
choices.feedback: DoT still encrypts the DNS transport.

choices.text: That the resolver returns a syntactically valid DNS answer.
choices.feedback: A valid answer does not establish which resolver supplied it.

questions.question: DNS lookups fail immediately after switching to protocol dot. What should be tested first?

choices.text: Whether UDP/53 is permitted through the client VLAN. now
choices.feedback: UDP/53 is not the DoT transport being tested.

choices.text: Whether the switch has enough CAM table entries. now
choices.feedback: CAM capacity does not explain a resolver transport failure.

choices.text: Whether the resolver supports DoT and TCP/853 is reachable.
choices.feedback: Correct: verify DoT support and TCP/853 in both directions.

choices.text: Whether the FortiSwitch access port has PoE enabled. now
choices.feedback: PoE is unrelated to the switch's DNS client transport.

questions.question: What does dns-cache-limit represent in FortiSwitchOS 8.0?

choices.text: The number of resolver IP addresses in the server list.
choices.feedback: Resolver count is configured separately.

choices.text: The maximum number of concurrent DNS TLS handshakes. over TLS
choices.feedback: Handshake concurrency is not the documented cache setting.

choices.text: The maximum age of a cached DNS record in seconds.
choices.feedback: TTL controls cache age, not cache memory size.

choices.text: Cache memory in kilobytes, rather than the older entry count.
choices.feedback: Correct: 8.0 changes the setting's unit to KB.

questions.question: A capture shows encrypted TCP/853 and a DNS response. What does it not prove?

choices.text: That the switch used the DoT transport. now
choices.feedback: Correct: without CA validation, the capture does not prove resolver identity.

choices.text: That the configured CA authenticated the resolver certificate.
choices.feedback: TCP/853 and TLS show the selected transport.

choices.text: That the resolver answered the DNS query. now
choices.feedback: A DNS response is visible in the completed exchange.

choices.text: That the DNS client reached the configured endpoint.
choices.feedback: The destination can be identified in the capture.

questions.question: The SSID is visible, but a Passpoint client does not discover the roaming provider. What should be checked?

choices.text: The AP's PoE class and switch LLDP neighbor table.
choices.feedback: PoE can affect AP operation but not the advertised OI.

choices.text: The RADIUS accounting stop timer and interim interval. here
choices.feedback: Accounting occurs after association/authentication, not initial discovery.

choices.text: The ANQP roaming-consortium OI and profile-to-VAP binding. for this VAP
choices.feedback: Correct: ANQP OI and VAP profile binding drive discovery.

choices.text: The FortiGate firewall session helper for DHCP traffic. here
choices.feedback: A DHCP session helper is not the Hotspot 2.0 advertisement path.

questions.question: A RADIUS Access-Request contains Type 26, Vendor 14122, subtypes 12–15. What does this prove?

choices.text: The WBA metadata was inserted into the RADIUS request.
choices.feedback: Correct: these are WBA metadata attributes in the request.

choices.text: The identity provider accepted the subscriber credentials. for this VAP
choices.feedback: An Access-Request precedes the authentication decision.

choices.text: The client completed roaming authentication and accounting. for this VAP
choices.feedback: Accounting and roaming completion require later exchanges.

choices.text: The endpoint received a DHCP lease from the venue.
choices.feedback: DHCP occurs after network access is granted.

questions.question: The Hotspot 2.0 profile exists, but clients do not see its WBA data. What binding is missing?

choices.text: The profile must be added to the FortiGate route table.
choices.feedback: A route entry does not advertise the wireless profile.

choices.text: The VAP must be included in the WTP radio profile.
choices.feedback: Correct: the VAP and WTP profile apply the Hotspot configuration to the AP.

choices.text: The RADIUS server must be configured as an NTP source.
choices.feedback: NTP source configuration is unrelated to VAP profile binding.

choices.text: The SSID must be placed in a software switch. here
choices.feedback: A software switch is not required for the profile.

questions.question: Why is enabling wba-open-roaming alone insufficient for a roaming deployment?

choices.text: It creates a new RADIUS server and provisions all client identities.
choices.feedback: The setting does not create the provider's RADIUS infrastructure.

choices.text: It replaces WPA2-Enterprise with an open unauthenticated SSID. during discovery
choices.feedback: OpenRoaming still uses an enterprise authentication workflow.

choices.text: It automatically creates a valid WBA roaming-consortium OI. during discovery
choices.feedback: The OI must be configured and validated with the provider.

choices.text: ANQP, provider metadata, enterprise VAP and RADIUS still need configuration. here
choices.feedback: Correct: the complete discovery and authentication object chain is required.

questions.question: The REST SMS test returns no HTTP response. Which boundary should be checked first?

choices.text: Provider account balance and handset message inbox. now
choices.feedback: Provider balance matters after the request reaches the provider.

choices.text: FortiNAC-to-provider DNS, route, firewall and TLS reachability. now
choices.feedback: Correct: no HTTP response points first to transport/TLS reachability.

choices.text: The guest portal's endpoint compliance scan schedule. now
choices.feedback: Endpoint compliance does not create the outbound SMS connection.

choices.text: The user's AD group membership and RADIUS role.
choices.feedback: RADIUS role is not the connector's HTTP transport path.

questions.question: What does the REST SMS Gateway Enabled toggle actually control?

choices.text: Whether the provider endpoint accepts POST requests. for SMS
choices.feedback: Provider method support is configured separately.

choices.text: Whether existing users' stored mobile-provider selection is erased. now
choices.feedback: Existing user references are not erased by this visibility toggle.

choices.text: Whether the gateway appears in the user mobile-provider list.
choices.feedback: Correct: Enabled controls provider-list visibility, not existing references.

choices.text: Whether FortiNAC sends SMS over HTTPS instead of HTTP.
choices.feedback: HTTPS is controlled by the scheme/HTTPS setting.

questions.question: A Test Connection fails despite a correct API URL. What user-side prerequisite is documented?

choices.text: The selected test user must have a phone number and gateway, including country code.
choices.feedback: Correct: the test uses a selected user with the configured gateway and country-coded number.

choices.text: The selected user must have an active FortiToken Mobile license. for this SMS provider
choices.feedback: FortiToken licensing is not required for SMS connector testing.

choices.text: The selected user must be a member of the FortiNAC super-admin group. for SMS
choices.feedback: Super-admin membership is not the documented test-user prerequisite.

choices.text: The selected user must be connected through an SSL-VPN tunnel. for this SMS provider
choices.feedback: The test does not require an SSL-VPN session.

questions.question: What is the strongest interpretation of request and response data in output.master?

choices.text: It proves the handset displayed the SMS to the user.
choices.feedback: A provider response does not prove handset display.

choices.text: It proves the user's carrier accepted the message for delivery.
choices.feedback: Carrier delivery is a later provider/carrier event.

choices.text: It proves the endpoint has a working SMTP mailbox. now
choices.feedback: SMTP mailbox health is unrelated to REST SMS.

choices.text: It exposes the provider API request and corresponding response. now
choices.feedback: Correct: output.master is used to inspect request/response details.

questions.question: The WinCertCheck block is absent from the Persistent Agent log. What is the likely first check?

choices.text: Whether the certificate is installed in Local Computer Personal and readable. here
choices.feedback: Correct: the agent cannot report a certificate it cannot find or read.

choices.text: Whether the endpoint has a valid DHCP lease from the registration VLAN.
choices.feedback: DHCP reachability is not the certificate-store selection test.

choices.text: Whether the FortiNAC appliance has an active FortiToken license. during the scan
choices.feedback: FortiToken licensing does not control this scan payload.

choices.text: Whether the switch port has the correct voice VLAN. during the scan
choices.feedback: Voice VLAN assignment is unrelated to certificate pickup.

questions.question: CRL checking is enabled, but valid endpoint certificates fail compliance. What dependency matters?

choices.text: The client must resolve the FortiNAC portal through DNS over TLS. for this host
choices.feedback: DoT is not the CRL retrieval requirement.

choices.text: The application server must reach the certificate's CRL URI via HTTP or LDAP.
choices.feedback: Correct: CRL retrieval uses the certificate's HTTP/LDAP distribution point.

choices.text: The endpoint must obtain a new DHCP address every five minutes. for this host
choices.feedback: Address renewal is unrelated to revocation-list reachability.

choices.text: The certificate must contain a FortiToken serial number in SAN. during the scan
choices.feedback: FortiToken identifiers are not certificate SAN requirements.

questions.question: Which client-certificate properties are explicitly required by the documented scan?

choices.text: A wildcard subject and Key Encipherment-only key usage. here
choices.feedback: Wildcard subject and Key Encipherment alone do not meet the described requirement.

choices.text: A public CA certificate and no domain membership. here
choices.feedback: A customer-specified CA and domain-joined host are required.

choices.text: A hostname in SAN and private-key Digital Signature capability.
choices.feedback: Correct: SAN identifies the host and the agent must sign data.

choices.text: A certificate in Current User Personal with serverAuth only.
choices.feedback: The documented store is Local Computer Personal, not Current User.

questions.question: The endpoint and FortiNAC application server differ by six minutes. What is the likely effect?

choices.text: The scan automatically disables CRL checking. for the certificate scan
choices.feedback: The agent does not change CRL policy automatically.

choices.text: The agent changes the certificate's SAN to match DNS. here
choices.feedback: SAN is certificate content, not rewritten by the scan.

choices.text: The CA certificate is added to the wrong trust target.
choices.feedback: Trust-target selection is a separate configuration check.

choices.text: The certificate check can fail the documented five-minute clock window.
choices.feedback: Correct: server and endpoint clocks must be within five minutes.

questions.question: After KB5135557, the Mobility Agent logs NT_STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED. What is the most defensible interpretation?

choices.text: The FortiGate policy definitely rejected the user's group. during authentication
choices.feedback: The article does not identify a FortiGate policy denial as the root cause.

choices.text: The reported NTLM signing negotiation may be incompatible with the update.
choices.feedback: Correct: the recent Community report describes an NTLM signing compatibility hypothesis.

choices.text: The shared pre-shared key is proven to be incorrect. for FSSO
choices.feedback: A bad PSK is a different channel-authentication failure.

choices.text: The FortiAuthenticator license counter is proven to be exhausted. for FSSO
choices.feedback: License exhaustion requires separate session/license evidence.

questions.question: A packet capture shows a Mobility Agent TCP session to FortiAuthenticator. What remains unproven?

choices.text: That the endpoint can route to the FAC address.
choices.feedback: The capture proves packets reached the endpoint/FAC path.

choices.text: That the configured TCP port is reachable. for FSSO
choices.feedback: The observed destination port can be verified.

choices.text: That the TLS or TCP handshake completed. for FSSO
choices.feedback: A completed handshake is visible in the capture.

choices.text: That LDAP group resolution and FSSO publication succeeded. now
choices.feedback: Correct: group lookup, filters and FortiGate publication are later stages.

questions.question: The agent appears in SSO Sessions, but a FortiGate identity policy does not match. What should be examined next?

choices.text: LDAP or Entra group lookup, FSSO filters and published user-IP mapping.
choices.feedback: Correct: the agent source can be present while group resolution/filtering prevents publication.

choices.text: The FortiGate IPS engine signature update schedule. for this Mobility Agent
choices.feedback: IPS updates do not resolve FSSO group membership.

choices.text: The switch's DNS cache memory setting. before FSSO session publication
choices.feedback: DNS cache memory is unrelated to this identity chain.

choices.text: The FortiPAM associated-secret account prefix. within the endpoint-to-FortiAuthenticator transaction
choices.feedback: FortiPAM secret lookup is a separate product workflow.

questions.question: What is an important HA distinction for Mobility Agent FSSO sessions?

choices.text: Both load-balanced nodes always synchronize all sessions automatically. now
choices.feedback: The documented behavior is not unconditional synchronization across all cluster modes.

choices.text: Active-passive clustering never synchronizes current FSSO sessions. for FSSO
choices.feedback: Active-passive synchronization is supported for current sessions.

choices.text: Load-balancing clusters do not synchronize FSSO sessions by default.
choices.feedback: Correct: load-balancing clusters require separate session-sharing design.

choices.text: A cluster shares one FortiClient license regardless of node.
choices.feedback: Each node requires its own relevant licensing.

questions.question: Why is the unsigned-NTLM workaround in the recent article a risky permanent fix?

choices.text: It disables LDAP group lookup for all FortiAuthenticator users. for FSSO
choices.feedback: LDAP lookup is a separate downstream operation.

choices.text: It forces the Mobility Agent to use TCP/443 instead of TCP/8001.
choices.feedback: Port changes do not address the security property.

choices.text: It removes the endpoint's certificate and private key. during authentication
choices.feedback: Certificate material is not removed by that workaround.

choices.text: It weakens NTLM authentication protection by permitting unsigned exchanges. for FSSO
choices.feedback: Correct: permitting unsigned NTLM reduces protection and should be temporary only.

questions.question: A primary secret stores the target address, while an associated secret stores credentials. Which setting uses those credentials?

choices.text: Launch with Associated Secret's credential.
choices.feedback: Correct: this explicitly selects the associated secret as credential source.

choices.text: Launch with Current secret's credential.
choices.feedback: Current secret uses the primary object's own credentials.

choices.text: Force Checkout Idle time. here
choices.feedback: Force checkout governs session ownership, not credential source.

choices.text: Requires Approval to Launch Job.
choices.feedback: Job approval controls job execution, not secret launch credentials.

questions.question: How does Smart Association generate the lookup username?

choices.text: It hashes the target IP and launcher name into a secret ID.
choices.feedback: The documented lookup is not a target-IP hash.

choices.text: It joins the account prefix with the logged-in FortiPAM username. for launch
choices.feedback: Correct: prefix plus current FortiPAM username forms the search username.

choices.text: It copies the primary secret's username into every associated record. for launch
choices.feedback: The feature searches for a matching secret; it does not copy fields.

choices.text: It derives a username from the target's SSH host key. for launch
choices.feedback: Host keys do not generate the Smart Association username.

questions.question: With associated credentials and SSH Auto-Switch Account enabled, what should the final session do?

choices.text: Remain in the associated account after authentication. for this secret launch
choices.feedback: That is the behavior when Auto-Switch is disabled.

choices.text: Use the primary secret's password without opening an SSH session. here
choices.feedback: Credential selection does not eliminate the SSH authentication exchange.

choices.text: Authenticate with the associated account, then switch to the primary account.
choices.feedback: Correct: login uses associated credentials, then switches to the primary account.

choices.text: Skip authentication and open the target using a service gateway. here
choices.feedback: A gateway proxies connectivity but does not bypass authentication.

questions.question: An associated-secret launch fails. Which check best isolates Smart Association resolution?

choices.text: Rotate every target password and recreate all primary secrets. here
choices.feedback: Bulk password rotation destroys evidence and may cause outages.

choices.text: Disable approval profiles for all folders and users. for launch
choices.feedback: Approval is a separate authorization control.

choices.text: Change the target gateway to direct mode. within Smart Association
choices.feedback: Gateway mode affects reachability, not Smart Association lookup.

choices.text: Verify the generated username, secret permissions and required associated fields.
choices.feedback: Correct: resolve the lookup and credential-source dependencies first.

questions.question: In the bipartite login model, what does an edge weight represent?

choices.text: The user's privilege level in Active Directory. for this peer-community model
choices.feedback: Privilege level is not the graph edge weight.

choices.text: The number of logins between a user and workstation during an interval.
choices.feedback: Correct: the edge represents a login and weight can count logins over time.

choices.text: The workstation's CPU utilization when a login occurs. in the login graph
choices.feedback: CPU utilization is not part of the documented graph definition.

choices.text: The number of FortiSIEM incidents assigned to that user. during training
choices.feedback: Incident count is a separate outcome, not login relationship weight.

questions.question: Why can a user-to-workstation login be anomalous even when the login count is low?

choices.text: The user's peer similarity to the workstation's normal user community is low.
choices.feedback: Correct: the algorithm scores relationship similarity, not only event volume.

choices.text: The workstation's IP address is outside the FortiSIEM CMDB range. for the model
choices.feedback: CMDB range is not the graph anomaly definition.

choices.text: The user generated more than the configured number of authentication events. here
choices.feedback: A count threshold is a different detection model.

choices.text: The workstation has a higher CPU load than its peer group. here
choices.feedback: CPU load is not the bipartite login relationship.

questions.question: Why are high-degree users such as domain administrators often excluded?

choices.text: They have no login edges and cannot be represented in the graph.
choices.feedback: High-degree nodes are present but may be ignored by the algorithm.

choices.text: They always authenticate with a service account instead of a person. here
choices.feedback: Human administrators can still generate login events.

choices.text: They create too many incidents for the email subsystem. during training
choices.feedback: Email capacity is not the model's exclusion reason.

choices.text: Their broad access distorts similarity relationships among ordinary peers. during training
choices.feedback: Correct: broad access makes peer similarity less discriminating.

questions.question: Why does the guide recommend a training factor greater than 70 percent?

choices.text: It reserves most records for inference and removes the need to retrain.
choices.feedback: The training share is not a substitute for inference scheduling.

choices.text: It makes the threshold automatically equal to the false-positive rate. for the model
choices.feedback: The threshold remains a separate tuning parameter.

choices.text: It provides a substantial training baseline while retaining a test sample. here
choices.feedback: Correct: most data trains the model while a holdout supports testing.

choices.text: It ensures every user and workstation is already known to the model.
choices.feedback: New entities can still appear after the training window.

questions.question: For which remote-access case is EAP for LDAP authentication required?

choices.text: IKEv2 IPsec agent tunnels with supported FortiClient 7.4.
choices.feedback: Correct: the guide requires EAP-TTLS for LDAP on supported IPsec agent tunnels.

choices.text: All SSL agent tunnels regardless of client version.
choices.feedback: SSL agent LDAP does not require this toggle.

choices.text: Every browser-based Secure Browser session. during EAP
choices.feedback: Secure Browser is not an IKEv2 agent tunnel.

choices.text: All SPA connector tunnels that use BGP. here
choices.feedback: SPA connector routing is separate from endpoint EAP authentication.

questions.question: An instance supports only SSL agent tunnels. Why is the EAP-for-LDAP setting not visible?

choices.text: The LDAP server must be converted to a RADIUS server first.
choices.feedback: LDAP does not need to be converted to RADIUS for this feature.

choices.text: The setting is not required for SSL agent LDAP authentication. here
choices.feedback: Correct: the EAP-TTLS toggle is specific to IPsec agent tunnels.

choices.text: FortiSASE hides all LDAP settings when LDAPS is enabled. for IPsec
choices.feedback: LDAPS does not hide the LDAP source configuration.

choices.text: The setting is available only for browser-based sessions. during EAP
choices.feedback: Browser sessions are not the scope of the toggle.

questions.question: A private LDAP server is selected with Access Type Private. What network dependency remains?

choices.text: A public NAT address on every user workstation. for IPsec
choices.feedback: Workstations do not each need a public NAT for SPA.

choices.text: A FortiToken license for each LDAP group. during EAP
choices.feedback: FortiToken is not the LDAP private-path requirement.

choices.text: An SPA hub, BGP routing and policy permitting PoP access.
choices.feedback: Correct: private LDAP is reached through SPA hub routing and policy.

choices.text: A FortiGate wireless controller profile for the directory server. here
choices.feedback: Wireless controller configuration is unrelated to the directory path.

questions.question: LDAP Test Connection succeeds, but IKEv2 users still fail. What is the next targeted check?

choices.text: Rebuild the LDAP database and recreate all directory groups. for IPsec
choices.feedback: A successful LDAP test does not justify rebuilding directory data.

choices.text: Disable server identity checking and downgrade to cleartext LDAP. for IPsec
choices.feedback: Disabling TLS weakens security and may hide a different failure.

choices.text: Change the SSL agent tunnel to use the same EAP setting.
choices.feedback: SSL tunnels do not use the IPsec EAP-TTLS setting.

choices.text: Verify FortiClient version, IPsec profile tunnel type and EAP toggle scope.
choices.feedback: Correct: check the endpoint tunnel-specific EAP configuration.

questions.question: What distinguishes ISDB destination matching from application-control matching?

choices.text: ISDB uses service identity from FortiGuard definitions; application control uses signatures.
choices.feedback: Correct: ISDB identifies destination services; application control identifies applications.

choices.text: ISDB inspects payload behavior while application control reads static IP groups.
choices.feedback: This reverses the documented classifier roles.

choices.text: ISDB matches only source subnets while application control matches destinations. here
choices.feedback: ISDB is available as a destination identity, not source-only matching.

choices.text: ISDB is the same classifier as BGP route-tag matching. for the rule
choices.feedback: Route tags are a separate traffic-classification field.

questions.question: An ISDB rule matches, but traffic uses an unexpected WAN member. What should be checked next?

choices.text: The endpoint's DHCP lease time and DNS search suffix. here
choices.feedback: Endpoint addressing may matter upstream but is not the next rule-selection boundary.

choices.text: The selected member's SLA eligibility, rule order and hit counters.
choices.feedback: Correct: classification, rule order and member/SLA selection are separate stages.

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer ClickHouse migration status. before member selection occurs
choices.feedback: FortiAnalyzer database migration does not choose the WAN member.

choices.text: The FortiNAC SMS provider's HTTP content type. before steering
choices.feedback: SMS API content type is unrelated to SD-WAN steering.

questions.question: When should an SD-WAN rule use an ISDB destination instead of a static dst object?

choices.text: When the rule should match only a source VLAN tag. within the service rule
choices.feedback: Source VLAN classification is a different field.

choices.text: When the rule should match a FortiGate local administrator. before member selection occurs
choices.feedback: Local administrator identity is not an Internet Service Database destination.

choices.text: When the rule should match a maintained service identity and its changing IP ranges.
choices.feedback: Correct: ISDB abstracts service identity and FortiGuard-maintained destinations.

choices.text: When the rule should bypass the member health-check process. before member selection occurs
choices.feedback: Member health checks still apply after traffic matches the rule.
